scenario_context.title: The Trial of Socrates
scenario_context.subtitle: Athens accuses Socrates of corrupting the youth and impiety against the gods.
scenario_context.image_caption: The city is divided between fear of chaos and loyalty to truth.
scenario_context.central_conflict_body: Should Socrates compromise to survive, or stay true to philosophy even when the city demands silence?
scenario_context.learning_goal_body: Understand moral integrity, justice, and the conflict between personal safety and truth.

socrates.cost: A verdict that could cost his life.

judge.name: Athenian Judge
judge.goal: Maintain public order and political stability.
judge.cost: Stability might suffocate freedom of thought.

student.name: Young Student
student.goal: Understand if philosophy is worth sacrificing for.

roleplay_situation.quote_body: ou are standing before the Athenian court. The judges offer a chance to apologize and stop teaching philosophy. If you accept, you may live. If you refuse, you may be punished severely.
roleplay_situation.callout: Will you protect your life, or defend your beliefs?
roleplay_situation.stake_body: Your legacy, the future of Athenian philosophy, and the meaning of public courage.

decision_selection.title: Choose Decision
decision_selection.subtitle: Each decision reveals a core value.
decision_selection.consequence_body: Your choice will shape the consequences and lessons.

refuse.title: Refuse to Apologize
refuse.principle: Truth is more important than survival

escape.title: Leave Athens
escape.principle: Freedom of thought needs space to live

consequence_result.immediate_consequence_body: The court views your stance as disobedient and dangerous.
consequence_result.philosophical_meaning_body: This choice shows that some may value truth and moral consistency over personal survival.

lesson_explanation.title: Lessons Learned
lesson_explanation.your_choice_shows_body: You chose {{title}}. This demonstrates a commitment to {{principle}}.

markdown.body_1: Socrates' decision shows the meaning of [[moral integrity]]: staying consistent with one's [[principles]], even under pressure.
markdown.quote: > An unexamined life is not worth living.
markdown.body_2: - A person with integrity does not only ask, **What will keep me safe?**
markdown.body_3: - They also ask, **What kind of person will I become if I betray what I believe?**
